message.content:
Let  
\[
V_1=x^2,\quad V_2=y^2,\quad V_3=z^2,\quad V_4=w^2
\]
and let
\[
a_1=1^2,\ a_2=3^2,\ a_3=5^2,\ a_4=7^2.
\]
The four equations are, for \(t=4,16,36,64\),
\[
\sum_{i=1}^4 \frac{V_i}{t-a_i}=1.
\]

Define
\[
Q(t)=\prod_{i=1}^4 (t-a_i)
\]
and
\[
P(t)=Q(t)\sum_{i=1}^4 \frac{V_i}{t-a_i}
=\sum_{i=1}^4 V_i\prod_{j\ne i}(t-a_j).
\]
Then at \(t=4,16,36,64\), we have \(P(t)=Q(t)\). Hence
\[
Q(t)-P(t)=(t-4)(t-16)(t-36)(t-64).
\]

The coefficient of \(t^3\) in \(P(t)\) is
\[
V_1+V_2+V_3+V_4=x^2+y^2+z^2+w^2.
\]
Now compute the coefficient of \(t^3\) in
\[
P(t)=Q(t)-(t-4)(t-16)(t-36)(t-64).
\]
For \(Q(t)\), the \(t^3\)-coefficient is
\[
-(1+9+25+49)=-84.
\]
For \((t-4)(t-16)(t-36)(t-64)\), the \(t^3\)-coefficient is
\[
-(4+16+36+64)=-120.
\]
Thus the \(t^3\)-coefficient of \(P(t)\) is
\[
-84-(-120)=36.
\]
Therefore,
\[
x^2+y^2+z^2+w^2=36.
\]

The answer is 36.
